reason: The only quote covers the new AMI or user data case; migrating to new instance types and moving from a launch configuration to a launch template appear only in unquoted context bullets.
Both quotes state an instance refresh replaces InService instances first and then instances in the warm pool.
The default-values table row for Instance warmup gives the default instance warmup if defined, otherwise the health check grace period.
The quotes state interface endpoints use PrivateLink to privately access the EC2 Auto Scaling APIs on the AWS network, with no internet gateway, NAT device or virtual private gateway needed.
Under 'Capacity Reservation types supported' the quote describes Interruptible Capacity Reservations with the same two sources and the 2-minute reclamation notice.
The quote states one launch configuration per group at a time, no modification after creation, and that you create a new one and update the group.
The quote states launch configurations cannot create groups with both Spot and On-Demand or multiple instance types, and a launch template is required.
The quote states accounts created on or after October 1, 2024 cannot create launch configurations by any method, listing the same four methods.
The quote states accounts created on or after June 1, 2023 cannot create launch configurations using the console.
The quote states that as of January 1, 2023 new EC2 instance types are no longer supported in launch configurations.
The quote gives the Pending, Pending:Wait, Pending:Proceed, InService sequence for an EC2_INSTANCE_LAUNCHING hook.
The quote says Auto Scaling 'tries to maintain' equivalent numbers by 'attempting to launch'; the claim drops this best-effort hedge and says it 'keeps' them equal.
The quote states the subnet with the highest number of available IP addresses is tried, and a failed attempt moves to another Availability Zone until it succeeds.
The quote states all launch template parameters are optional but a missing AMI cannot be added when creating the group.
That later launches use the service-linked role's permissions is stated only in the unquoted sentence before the first quote; the quotes alone do not state it.
The quote lists Systems Manager parameters (AMI ID), Capacity Reservations, Capacity Blocks and Dedicated Hosts as newer features available with launch templates.

The quotes state instances get a role through an instance profile chosen in the launch template or configuration, and iam:PassRole is needed to create or update a group with a template that specifies an instance profile.
The quote states a launch template, instead of a launch configuration, allows multiple versions.
The quotes state LaunchInstances only works with groups that use launch templates and launch configurations are not supported.
The quotes state each LaunchInstances call can only target one Availability Zone and mixed instances policies must be fully On-Demand or fully Spot.
The quotes state ALB, NLB and GWLB are attached through a target group, and Classic Load Balancer instances are registered directly with the load balancer.
The quote states launched instances are registered and terminated instances deregistered automatically, without registering individual instances.
The quote states the default EC2-health-check-only replacement and that ELB health checks, when turned on, let it replace instances a load balancer reports unhealthy.
The quote names the four load balancer types that can be used with an Auto Scaling group.
The quote states the load balancer does not route traffic to registered targets in Availability Zones not enabled for it.
The quote gives the launch and terminate meanings of continue and abandon, including that abandon stops remaining lifecycle hooks.
The DefaultResult parameter is the action taken on timeout or unexpected failure, and its default value is ABANDON.
The quote states console-added hooks send to EventBridge by default and direct SNS, SQS or Lambda targets need the CLI, CloudFormation or an SDK.
The quotes recommend EventBridge instead of SNS or SQS and state that the SNS and SQS notifications contain the same information.
The quote lists four notification target approaches: EventBridge, SNS, SQS and Lambda.
The quote states the global timeout is the maximum wait-state time: 48 hours or 100 times the heartbeat timeout, whichever is smaller.
The API reference states the HeartbeatTimeout default is 3600 seconds (1 hour), and the user guide confirms one hour.
Under the HeartbeatTimeout parameter the quote states the range is 30 to 7200 seconds.
The document history row dated July 28, 2025 adds direct Lambda targets, and the guide quotes give the CLI, CloudFormation or SDK requirement and the console EventBridge default.
The quote calls this a popular use: a launch hook ensures bootstrap scripts finished and apps are ready before registration with the load balancer at the end of the hook.
Under 'Lifecycle hook availability' the footnote states hooks do not apply to attach or detach, standby moves, or force delete.
The quote states hooks perform a custom action on lifecycle events and give a specified time, one hour by default, before the next state.
The quote is one bullet under 'As an example of using lifecycle hooks'; the claim states EventBridge notification as general behavior, but SNS, SQS or Lambda can also be targets.
The quote states a new instance is not counted in aggregated metrics until it is InService and its instance warmup has finished.
The quote states a lifecycle hook does not prevent Spot termination when capacity is gone, which can happen at any time with a two-minute interruption notice.
